newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Main provisions of the EU working time directive.
newsitem.headline: Main provisions of the EU working time directive.

text.p: The European Union's working time directive, which was upheld by the European Court of Justice on Tuesday, sets the following rules to protect worker health and safety:

-- An average maximum work week of 48 hours, including overtime. The average can be based on a period of up to four months. For at least seven years, governments can opt out of this provision as long as they ensure that any work beyond 48 hours is done on a voluntary basis and employers keep good records.
-- A minimum daily rest period of 11 consecutive hours.
-- A minimum uninterrupted rest period of 24 hours per week. The court struck down a provision requiring the rest period to in principle include Sunday.
-- Paid annual leave of at least four weeks. Governments may wait for three years to apply this as long as workers are guaranteed three weeks of paid leave.
-- An average shift of eight hours for night workers.

Workers in a wide range of transport sectors, seafarers and doctors in training are not covered by the rules. Governments may also introduce flexible arrangements for a range of workers including managing executives, employees in the home, religious officials, health care workers, journalists and utilities and emergency-services workers.
